newsitem.title: JAPAN: Okinawa refineries to step up oil product exports.
newsitem.headline: Okinawa refineries to step up oil product exports.

text.p: Refineries in Japan's southernmost island of Okinawa said on Tuesday they would step up exports of oil products following upcoming export deregulation in a bid to capitalise on surplus production capacity.

"We would like to shift our emphasis from third-party processing to product exports once (oil product) exports are deregulated," said an official with Okinawa Sekiyu Seisei Co Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd.
"Exporting oil products can be more profitable," he said.

Third party processing for Asian countries such as South Korea and Taiwan has accounted for 50 percent to 70 percent of production at Okinawan refineries as their processing capacity greatly exceeds local demand, refinery officials said.

But that percentage is likely to shrink, refiners say, as government deregulation expected to be implemented by September eases export rules in order to encourage a more liberalized market and give refiners greater operational flexibility.

In third-party arrangements, profits from product sales are divided by refiners and the companies that supply crude oil and later market the refined products, while oil product exporters keep all the profit from their own product sales.

But Okinawa refineries had traditionally been inactive in product exports until only recently due to strict government regulations and a cumbersome application proccess. Currently oil firms are required to gain a government approval each time they intend to export oil products.
It usually takes about a week before the government grants approval, a trader with a refinery said.

Specific deregulation measures are currently under discussion by a government panel, and details cannot be revealed, said an official for the Agency of Natural Resources and Energy, which supervises exports of oil products.
The export approval process, however, is scheduled to be simplified by September, refiners say.
Ahead of the planned deregulation, refineries in Okinawa have already started exporting part of their naphtha and gas oil production.
Okinawa Sekiyu exported gas oil to Guam last December, and to China in January on a spot basis.
General Sekiyu KK, which has a 87.5 percent stake in Nansei Sekiyu, started exporting light, or paraffinic, naphtha cargoes to China earlier this year.
"This is like a trial-run for us ahead of the deregulation," a General Sekiyu spokesman said.
The company, owned 49 percent by Exxon Corp, plans to start gas oil exports from Okinawa after the deregulation, he added.
Together Okinawa Sekiyu and Nansei Sekiyu KK, the other refinery on the island, have a combined processing capacity of 210,000 barrel-per-day.
